findings.text: _apply_descope_reason_edits is a second copy of the keyed head-meta read-modify-write that reckon/_store_section_ops.py:490 apply_section_dependency_edits already owns, and it is placed in a different module, so the next fix to that pattern has to be made in two places; the two do differ in value type (a reason string against a ref list) and both reuse reckon/_plan_html.py:2074 _set_meta and :2087 _remove_meta, so this is duplication of the orchestration rather than of the primitive.

the third case asserts only that the refusal text contains the literal '{"status": "descoped", "reason":', so it stays green if the refusal names a form the store rejects; the claim in its own name, that the named form works, rests entirely on the first case and is not asserted here.

the docstring claims an edit lands on the reasons already on the page rather than replacing its siblings, and no test asserts that claim: each of the four cases performs exactly one write on a plan that carries no reasons meta. I verified the claim by probe (two sequential reasoned descopes on a recordless plan leave both reasons in the map), but the behaviour is unguarded by any committed assertion.

the ruff figure of 28 is the line count of --output-format=concise, which includes ruff's own two summary lines; the finding count is 26 at both the base and the head revision (my measurement), and the new test adds none because it passes every check. The conclusion stands and the quoted number does not.

the helper docstring names an external project ('a plan shaped like nova's') in reckon's own source, against the repo-agnostic rule that reckon carries no project name; the fixture is synthesised and the name adds provenance the reader does not need.
